sector_news_last_month: Nifty Auto traded close to its 52-week highs through much of July, ranking among the stronger-performing NSE sectoral indices for the month
Monthly retail sales data from the industry dealers' body showed a record month for overall vehicle sales, with passenger-vehicle sales also posting strong year-on-year growth

Electric passenger-vehicle registrations crossed a fresh volume milestone for the first time, more than doubling year-on-year, with several manufacturers reporting their highest-ever monthly EV retail sales
Industry participants linked accelerating demand for electric, hybrid and CNG vehicles partly to fuel-price increases stemming from the escalating West Asia conflict
Q1 FY27 earnings season ran through the month for several auto names, though a number of major results - including for two large manufacturers - were scheduled just after the period closed
A recurring theme across earnings previews was margin pressure from higher steel, aluminium and copper costs, even as revenue and volume growth remained strong across the sector
Festive-season demand optimism was repeatedly cited by market participants as a key driver of buying interest, particularly in two-wheeler and SUV-focused names
One major two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer's share buyback opened and closed during the month, supporting sentiment in that stock

Broader market volatility tied to the US-Iran conflict and swings in crude oil prices repeatedly spilled over into auto-sector sentiment, with easing tensions later in the month improving risk appetite and lifting auto shares
Passenger-vehicle market-share rankings shifted during the quarter, with one major manufacturer's passenger-vehicle arm reclaiming a top market position from a rival

Auto-ancillary and component names showed some of the sharpest single-session moves in the sector, reflecting more stock-specific and news-driven trading than the broader passenger-vehicle and two-wheeler names
